output.reason: The brief is convincing. It backs its diagnosis with specific new evidence: about 11% of unused Pellacott 2026 valves leaked in Brenmoor's own lab tests, compared with 1% for Pellacott's 2025 valves and none for Durrant-Hale. Claim rates are the same across installer and firmware groups. The leak-test rig has been out of service since January. The 2026 certificates repeat the same few sets of values. It explains why the score went up anyway and lists clear next steps. It loses points because it doesn't say what to do about next week's line stoppage, beyond requiring Brenmoor's own helium testing before any stock is released.
